title: Reach Power Signs CRADA with U.S. Army to Advance Vehicle-Integrated Wireless Power for Autonomous Drones
summary: Reach signs a U.S. Army CRADA to evaluate vehicle-mounted wireless power for longer drone endurance and persistent autonomous operations.
body_markdown:
## Collaboration with DEVCOM Ground Vehicle Systems Center will evaluate wireless power technology for extending small drone endurance and supporting persistent autonomous operations


November 19, 2026 — Redwood City, Calif., – Reach Power ([Reach](https://www.reachpower.com/) ), a leader in wireless power-at-a-distance, today announced a Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) with the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Ground Vehicle Systems Center (GVSC). The collaboration will evaluate vehicle-mounted wireless power technology designed to extend the endurance of small uncrewed aerial systems (sUAS).


The collaboration will explore how vehicle-mounted wireless power systems can support persistent drone operations by[delivering energy to sUAS while in flight](https://reachpower.com/news/wireless-powered-drone-10-hour-flight/) , potentially reducing the need for frequent landings, battery swaps, and recharging.


Under the agreement, Reach will provide its beamforming technology in a form factor suitable for integration with a Valinor Dispatch drone dock and a Red Cat Black Widow short-range reconnaissance (SRR) drone. Reach will also provide technical specifications and integration support for mounting the technology on a government-provided military vehicle.


The evaluation will include integrating a virtual representation of the technology into GVSC’s Virtual Experimentation (VE) and training simulation software to explore concepts of operations (CONOPS) and assess the operational value of wireless power. The collaboration will also investigate wireless power delivery to remote ground sensors.


“Autonomous drones have tremendous potential to transform battlefield awareness, but their effectiveness is still limited by battery endurance,” said Chris Davlantes, Founder and CEO of Reach. “By integrating wireless power directly into military vehicles, we can turn those platforms into mobile sources of energy for autonomous systems, enabling persistent ISR and reducing the logistical burden of keeping drones operational.”


### **Enabling Persistent Autonomy for Army Ground Forces**


Small drones are becoming increasingly important to military operations, providing intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), force protection, and improved situational awareness. However, limited battery endurance requires frequent recovery, recharging, or battery replacement, interrupting operations and increasing demands on personnel.


Reach’s technology uses highly controlled radio-frequency (RF) power beaming to deliver energy to compatible receivers at a distance. When integrated with military vehicles, the technology has the potential to support airborne drones throughout missions, allowing ground forces to maintain persistent surveillance without relying solely on onboard batteries.


The CRADA will provide a framework for GVSC to evaluate vehicle-mounted wireless power, examine potential integration approaches, and explore operational concepts for extending small-drone endurance.


The collaboration builds on Reach’s broader work with the Department of Defense to develop wireless power capabilities for autonomous aircraft, ground systems, and distributed sensors, including projects supported by the Operational Energy Capability Improvement Fund (OECIF).


As defense forces increase their use of autonomous systems, the ability to sustain those systems without frequent human intervention will become increasingly important. Wireless power offers a potential infrastructure layer for persistent autonomy, with applications extending beyond military drones to robotics, distributed sensing, and other autonomous platforms.
